title: A transferable, predictive virtual cell

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a computational model that integrates molecular processes well enough to predict whole-cell behavior under previously untested perturbations and conditions. It would connect changes inside a cell to outcomes such as growth, survival, division and recovery, while also predicting how molecular states evolve over time. The defining ambition is transfer: useful predictions would extend beyond the cell types and conditions used to construct or train the model. This describes a target capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Conceptual synthesis: an integrated simulation and a transferable predictive instrument are different accomplishments. A model may reproduce a particular cell’s behavior under familiar conditions without reliably forecasting a new intervention or working in a substantially different cell. A convincing virtual cell would therefore need both integration of cellular processes and evidence that its predictions remain useful when the biological setting changes.

significance.text: Conditional impact assessment: if this predictive reliability were achieved, a virtual cell could become an experimental instrument for cell biology. Researchers could explore genetic changes, chemical exposures and environmental conditions computationally before selecting physical experiments. Its direct contribution would be better experimental prioritization and more explicit predictions about the consequences of interventions, including combinations that would be costly to examine exhaustively in the laboratory.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more efficient investigation of cellular mechanisms and better selection of interventions for subsequent testing. These benefits would depend on performance in the relevant biological setting, the quality of the available inputs and the model’s ability to recognize uncertainty. A convincing cellular model would not automatically yield predictive tissues, patients or organisms: interactions among cells, spatial organization and organism-level physiology would remain further modeling and validation challenges. The analogy to a computational laboratory is useful only within the model’s demonstrated predictive boundaries.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is reliable prediction across both unfamiliar interventions and substantially different cells. Integrating many processes into one simulation is part of that goal, but predictive transfer requires more: the model must capture relationships that remain useful when an intervention changes the system or when the cellular context differs from its development data. The supplied scientific material does not establish how close existing work is to this target or verify that the full capability remains absent as of November 1, 2026.

Proposed technical barriers include poorly measured reactions, feedback, stochasticity and state-dependent interactions. These raise distinct modeling problems: incomplete measurements can leave several explanations compatible with the same observations; feedback can alter the consequences of an intervention over time; stochastic behavior can require predictions of outcome distributions rather than one trajectory; and an interaction observed in one cellular state may behave differently in another. These are explanatory engineering considerations drawn from the proposed concept, not findings verified by the retained source.

Engineering synthesis: the model would also need to distinguish uncertainty caused by biological variability from uncertainty caused by missing inputs or inadequate knowledge. A useful instrument should identify when the supplied information cannot support a reliable prediction. Establishing that boundary is part of the capability, alongside improving prediction accuracy.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes to Thornburg and colleagues a paper titled “Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D,” dated March 9, 2026, with DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009. It reports a simulation of the approximately 100-minute cell cycle of the minimal bacterium JCVI-syn3A, integrating genetic processes, metabolism, growth and division. These details preserve the research’s account of a potentially important whole-cell simulation, but the supplied review could not verify the article identity, date or scientific results from the retained source content. The approximately 100-minute duration and listed integrated processes therefore remain reported, unverified details.

According to the supplied review, the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access message and no article-specific scientific text. The earlier description of the evidence as abstract-level support must therefore be withdrawn: no abstract is available in that artifact. The research also reports an earlier publisher 403 response, but the supplied review found no retained record that substantiates it. A complete extraction of the captured access message does not establish that the article itself was captured or inspected.

The available record consequently establishes no verified demonstration of the reported simulation and provides no basis for determining whether that study tested transfer across diverse cells or previously unseen interventions. This access limitation is not evidence that the reported result is false. Even if the described simulation were confirmed, its relationship to the broader target would depend on its actual predictive evaluation; a simulation of one minimal bacterium would not, by itself, establish transferable prediction. The supplied review also records an empty freshness search record, so developments through November 1, 2026 cannot be assessed from these inputs.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: freeze the model and prospectively predict unseen single and combined genetic, chemical and environmental interventions in several substantially different cell types. The evaluation should distinguish predictions within familiar cellular settings from transfer to cells outside those used for model construction or training. Independent experiments would then measure time-resolved molecular states, growth or survival, and recovery, allowing the predictions to be assessed against both intermediate cellular responses and eventual outcomes.
completion_criteria.label: Frozen model prospectively predicts interventions across unfamiliar cell types

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation requirements: specify accuracy targets, acceptable uncertainty and meaningful cell-type diversity before observing the test results. Predictions should outperform simple baselines, with performance reported separately across cell types, intervention classes, combinations and time horizons. Uncertainty should be declared in advance and checked against observed errors. The evaluation should also define what constitutes insufficient input and test whether the model identifies those cases. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards; the supplied material does not resolve their numerical thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Predictions outperform baselines under prespecified accuracy and uncertainty criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent groups should be able to reproduce the evaluation using documented model versions, inputs, experimental protocols and analysis procedures. Reports should state the measurements, computation and cell-specific adaptation needed to obtain useful predictions, because transfer requiring extensive rebuilding is a different practical accomplishment from transfer with limited additional information. Successful finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth across the tested settings, not literal universality across all cells or interventions.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication documents transfer resource requirements and demonstrated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based conceptual comparison: BIF-08, “Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates,” has the closest stated overlap. It focuses on cellular states and their future trajectories or fates, while BIF-03 seeks the broader ability to predict whole-cell behavior under interventions. Fate forecasting could contribute to a virtual cell, but success at forecasting fates would not alone demonstrate the integrated, transferable intervention predictions sought here.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” BIF-02, “Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence,” BIF-06, “A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions,” and BIF-09, “Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities,” concern components or inputs that could support a virtual cell. Regulatory effects, molecular behavior, functional assignments and interaction strengths address different levels of biological description. Accurate component predictions would still need to be integrated and validated at the level of cellular outcomes.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” overlaps through the relationships needed to predict responses to interventions. Reconstructing a causal network and producing quantitatively accurate, time-resolved whole-cell predictions remain distinct goals. BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” focus on designing biological systems; a virtual cell could help evaluate proposed designs, but predictive modeling does not itself demonstrate that a designed genome, circuit or pathway will function when built.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” concerns molecular organization at a broader biological scale; such maps could supply context without establishing cellular dynamics under intervention. BIF-11, “Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes,” addresses reconstruction of genomic inputs rather than prediction of cellular behavior. BIF-12, “Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities,” extends to community composition and function, where interactions among organisms introduce a further scale beyond an individual virtual cell.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” concerns the breadth and autonomy of a discovery workflow. Such a system might use a virtual cell to generate or evaluate hypotheses, while a virtual cell could operate as a specialized instrument without autonomous discovery capabilities. These entries therefore describe complementary capabilities rather than interchangeable innovations.

brief.title: A computer model that predicts how different cells behave
possible: Researchers could try a genetic change, chemical exposure or change in a cell’s surroundings on a computer before testing it in the laboratory. The model would predict changes inside the cell and whether it would grow, survive, divide or recover—even for interventions and cell types it had not learned from.
why: Cell biologists could choose experiments with a clearer idea of what to expect. They could explore combinations too costly to test exhaustively, helping them investigate how cells work and select interventions for laboratory testing.

sources.who: Zane R. Thornburg, Zaida Luthey-Schulten and colleagues
sources.showed: They simulated a minimal bacterium’s complete life cycle, linking molecular activity to growth, shape and division. The model reproduced experimental measurements and predicted differences between offspring.
sources.quote: We predict not only the average behavior of partitioning to daughter cells but also the heterogeneity among them.
sources.cited_for: It supports linking molecular processes with the behavior of a whole cell.
sources.not_established: Simulating a minimal bacterium does not establish reliable predictions for unfamiliar interventions or substantially different cells.

sources.who: Jonathan R. Karr, Markus W. Covert and colleagues
sources.showed: They built a whole-cell model of a bacterium, combining its molecular processes. They tested predictions against independent measurements spanning molecular activity and cell behavior.
sources.quote:
Our whole-cell model accounts for all annotated
gene functions and was validated against a broad
range of data.
sources.cited_for: It supports integrating cellular processes and testing the resulting predictions against experiments.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish prediction across substantially different cell types.

sources.who: Yusuf Roohani, Kexin Huang and Jure Leskovec
sources.showed: Their model, GEARS, predicted gene expression—how active genes are—after unfamiliar genetic changes and combinations. It outperformed comparison methods in their tests.
sources.quote:
GEARS is able to predict outcomes of perturbing
combinations consisting of genes that were never experimentally
perturbed.
sources.cited_for: It supports predicting responses to genetic changes absent from training.
sources.not_established: Reliable prediction required training in the same cell type or condition; gene activity alone does not establish whole-cell behavior.

sources.who: Constantin Ahlmann-Eltze, Wolfgang Huber and Simon Anders
sources.showed: They compared deep learning models with simple prediction rules. For combined genetic changes, all tested models had larger errors than a rule that added the effects of the individual changes.
sources.cited_for: It supports requiring complex models to beat simple alternatives in meaningful tests.
sources.not_established: These tests assess gene activity after genetic changes, not transferable prediction of whole-cell behavior.

shown: Thornburg and colleagues simulated a minimal bacterium’s complete life cycle and reproduced several experimental measurements. Karr and colleagues also integrated molecular processes into a bacterial model and tested it against independent data.

Roohani and colleagues predicted gene activity after unfamiliar genetic changes with GEARS. Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues found that tested deep learning models, including GEARS, did not consistently beat simple alternatives. Reliable prediction across substantially different cells remains to be demonstrated.
missing: A fixed model would need to predict unfamiliar genetic, chemical and environmental changes across substantially different cell types.
Predictions would need to connect molecular changes over time with growth, survival and recovery.
The model would need to beat simple alternatives and recognize when its inputs cannot support a reliable prediction.
Independent groups would need to reproduce useful transfer and document the measurements, computing and adaptation it requires.

milestones.label: A fixed model predicts interventions across unfamiliar cell types
milestones.explanation: A fixed model would have to predict unseen interventions and combinations across different cells before experiments measure molecular changes and outcomes over time. This would test transfer beyond familiar settings.

milestones.label: Predictions beat simple alternatives under agreed criteria
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to set accuracy, uncertainty and cell-diversity criteria in advance, assess missing inputs and show gains over simple alternatives. This would establish when predictions deserve confidence.

milestones.label: Independent groups reproduce transfer and establish its practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent groups would have to reproduce results using documented procedures and report required measurements, computing and cell-specific changes. This would establish practical usefulness and demonstrated limits.

uncertain: How accurate must predictions be, and how different must the tested cells be, to count as useful transfer?
How much rebuilding for each cell type is compatible with a transferable model?
Can models distinguish natural biological variability from uncertainty caused by missing measurements or incomplete knowledge?

page.title: Virtual cells with cross-context generalization
page.definition: A computational cell model predicts molecular changes over time and cellular growth, survival and division after genetic, chemical or environmental perturbations, meaning imposed changes. Predictions transfer to perturbations and cell types absent from model construction or training.

goal.need: GEARS used 102 single-gene and 128 two-gene perturbations to predict 5,151 gene pairs. Such predictions address the combinatorial cost of choosing interventions for laboratory testing.

figures.caption: The combination space explored in GEARS Figure 4
figures.note: The 5,151 pairs are the prediction space, not the number experimentally validated.

statements.quote: virtual cells that can transfer information across datasets and conditions, serve multiple queries concurrently, and unify data from different modalities.
statements.context: The organisation identifies these capabilities as its goal for a general-purpose model.

statements.quote: The ability for models to generalize to new cell contexts is ultimately key to unlocking virtual cells for drug discovery
statements.context: Dave Burke, Arc’s chief technology officer, describes the objective of the Virtual Cell Challenge.

statements.quote: universal cell models with sufficient biological complexity to predict how any cell responds to an intervention
statements.context: Nicole Kleinstreuer describes the goal in Biohub’s announcement of collaboration with NIH and the Department of Energy.

completion.title: A fixed virtual-cell model passes independent prospective tests across unseen cell types and perturbations.
completion.criterion: A fixed model jointly predicts molecular trajectories and cellular growth, division and survival after unseen genetic, chemical and environmental perturbations, including combinations, in cell types excluded from development. Independent prospective laboratory experiments reproduce its advantage over no-change, mean-response and applicable additive baselines for the tested contexts and readouts. Unperturbed measurements may initialize a new cell type. This is a provisional capability test; the cited documents supply no universal error tolerance or required number of cell types.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional synthesis of published developer goals and evaluation proposals.
completion.basis: Searched CZI’s virtual-cell roadmap, Arc’s 2025–2026 challenge definitions, Valence/Recursion’s capability levels and GenBio’s validation proposal for a joint completion test. None defines a pass criterion covering molecular dynamics, cellular outcomes and transfer to unseen cells and interventions. This synthesis combines their stated capabilities with prospective validation and comparison against simple baselines.

milestones.title: A whole-cell model predicts mutant growth within a band four wild-type standard deviations wide.
milestones.criterion: Apply Karr et al.’s Figure 7A agreement test to predicted and measured growth-rate pairs: the agreement band has a total width of four standard deviations of the wild-type growth measurement. On 20 July 2012, the authors reported measurements for 12 single-gene disruption strains of Mycoplasma genitalium; two-thirds of the predictions met their agreement criterion. The paper sets no minimum fraction of mutants that a general whole-cell model must predict correctly.
milestones.set_by: Karr et al., experimental validation protocol in Figure 7A; a study-specific agreement test.
milestones.threshold_quote: the region has a width of four times the SD of the wild-type strain growth measurement.

milestones.title: A whole-cell model simulates a complete cell cycle and reproduces measured cellular physiology.
milestones.criterion: Integrate genetic information processing, metabolism, growth and division in a spatial simulation, and recover measured cellular properties. On 9 March 2026, Thornburg et al. reported the approximately 100-minute cycle of JCVI-syn3A, recovering doubling time, messenger-RNA half-lives, protein distributions, ribosome counts and the DNA origin-to-terminus ratio. This is an organism-specific demonstration; its abstract supplies neither a numerical agreement cutoff nor the number of simulated cells.
milestones.set_by: Thornburg et al., published integration and validation demonstration for JCVI-syn3A; not a general accuracy standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: We simulate the complete cell cycle in 4D (space and time), including all genetic information processes, metabolic networks, growth, and cell division.

milestones.title: A model lowers expression-prediction error when neither perturbed target appeared in training.
milestones.criterion: Use GEARS’s two-of-two-unseen split and mean-squared error on the 20 most changed genes. Its evaluation used 131 two-gene perturbations; GEARS reported 53% improvement in the class with both targets unseen. The 2025 reanalysis found all tested models worse than an additive baseline for double perturbations under its different protocol. These are benchmark-specific findings.
milestones.set_by: Roohani et al., GEARS evaluation protocol, Figure 2e–f.
milestones.threshold_quote: both genes (two of two unseen) have not been seen individually perturbed at the time of training

milestones.title: A model ranks first in Arc’s six-cell-line zero-shot prediction challenge.
milestones.criterion: Rank first under Arc’s 2026 aggregate of six metrics. Predict gene-expression responses to CRISPR-interference gene repression in six cell lines: three for validation and three for final testing. Only unperturbed target-context profiles and target-gene identifiers are supplied; perturbation responses are withheld. This is a relative prize criterion. The 2025 Generalist Prize went to Altos Labs across seven metrics after H1 stem-cell fine-tuning; that organiser-reported result is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Arc Institute, 2026 Virtual Cell Challenge task and prize evaluation; written for human cell lines.
milestones.threshold_quote: final rankings use an aggregate across a broader panel of six metrics

milestones.title: Virtual cells predict and explain core cellular responses across environments and over time.
milestones.criterion: Meet Valence/Recursion’s proposed VC level 2: predict and explain functional responses of core biology across environmental variation and over time. Core biology means processes observable across measurement modalities. No numerical accuracy cutoff is specified. On 9 September 2026, Sun et al. reported ProteinTalks using over 38 million temporal protein-abundance measurements, with drug-response prediction and transfer to organoids and biopsies. This supports a proteomic component; it does not establish the entire proposed level.
milestones.set_by: Valence Labs and Recursion, proposed evaluation framework, section 3.4; a developer proposal in a preprint, not an adopted community standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: VC level 2. Predicts and explains functional response for core biology, across environmental variation, and over time.

milestones.title: Laboratory experiments confirm a multiscale virtual cell’s novel intervention predictions.
milestones.criterion: Confirm novel predictions of multi-step, multiscale cellular responses in new laboratory experiments within developed cell contexts. GenBio identifies novel-prediction wet-lab validation as its test without specifying numerical tolerances. On 18 August 2026 it reported AIDO Cell prototypes for K-562 and Hep-G2 and leading performance on 24 of 31 benchmark metrics, while describing novel-prediction experiments as underway. These are developer-reported results, not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: GenBio AI, AIDO Cell development and validation statement of 18 August 2026; written for its human-cell prototypes.
milestones.threshold_quote: wet-lab validation on novel predictions is the ultimate test.

not_found: No independent prospective demonstration jointly satisfying the completion criterion was located.
No final ranking for the 2026 Virtual Cell Challenge was found as of 14 November 2026.
The Ahlmann-Eltze benchmark’s full text could not be reopened at PMC or Nature.
GenBio’s technical whitepaper could not be opened from its public announcement; access was offered by request.

results.finding: A JCVI-syn3A whole-cell model simulated the approximately 100-minute cell cycle; the number of simulated cells was not stated.
results.detail: The spatial model integrated genetic processes, metabolism, growth and division and recovered measured cellular properties.
results.quote: The model captures the origin-to-terminus ratio measured in our DNA sequencing and recovers other experimental measurements, such as doubling time, mRNA half-lives, protein distributions, and ribosome counts.

results.finding: For 12 single-gene disruption strains, two-thirds of predicted growth rates agreed with measurements.
results.detail: The Figure 7A agreement band had a total width of four wild-type growth-measurement standard deviations.
results.quote:
We found that two-
thirds of the predictions were consistent with the measured
growth rates.

results.finding: The model simulated 128 wild-type cells and reproduced measured doubling time and other cellular properties.
results.detail: The model integrated metabolism, genetic information processing, growth and division, but the supplied text does not establish a spatial simulation as required by the criterion.
results.quote:
We simulated 128 wild-type cells in a typical
Mycoplasma culture environment, with each simulation predict-
ing not only cellular properties such as the cell mass and growth
rate but also molecular properties including the count, localiza-
tion, and activity of each molecule

results.finding: GEARS reported 53% improvement for two unseen targets in a dataset of 131 two-gene perturbations.
results.detail: The evaluation used mean-squared error on the 20 most differentially expressed genes. The number of perturbations in the two-unseen class is not stated.
results.quote:
GEARS improves performance 
by more than 30% across all cases (Fig. 2f), with the highest improve-
ment of 53% observed when both perturbed genes in the combination 
are unseen.

results.finding: For 62 held-out double perturbations, all tested models had higher expression-prediction error than the additive baseline.
results.detail: The models were trained on all single perturbations, so both targets had appeared individually in training. The primary metric was L2 distance for the 1,000 most highly expressed genes, rather than the specified two-of-two-unseen split and top-20-gene MSE.

results.finding: AttentionPert achieved a top-20-gene MSE of 0.159 across 9 two-gene perturbations with both targets unseen.
results.detail: On Norman dataset Split 1, AttentionPert's MSE was 0.159 versus 0.219 for GEARS. The full dataset contained 131 two-gene perturbations; the reported unseen-target test class contained nine.
results.quote: Among them, AttentionPert outperforms GEARS on all nine perturbations of the hardest seen 0/2 scenario.

results.finding: ProteinTalks predicts drug responses using more than 38 million temporal protein-abundance measurements.
results.detail: The model transfers to patient-derived organoids and clinical biopsies and provides protein-level interpretations. This supports a proteomic component of the milestone but does not establish level 2 across core biology and measurement modalities.
results.quote: Here we generated more than 38 million temporal protein-abundance measurements from systematically perturbed breast cancer cell lines, and developed ProteinTalks, a virtual cell model.
